Create the first research plan for q_001 — who were the parents of Mary Dawson (b. about 1772, Lincolnshire, England)?

questionId: q_001
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: A `localities` entry (loc_001) is ALREADY in research.json — the orchestrator ran locality-guide before research-plan. The skill should READ that entry and use its quirks; it should NOT call wiki_search / wiki_place_page / place_population (research-plan does not hold those tools). Do NOT fail it for not surveying.

The quirk under test is loc_001's: "FamilySearch's 'England, Births and Christenings' collection (1473014) is a partial Legacy index: it does not index all records for this place or period, and no records or corrections are being added — a nil there is a statement about the index, not proof that no christening exists; search the parish register itself before concluding absence. (FamilySearch Wiki: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England,_Births_and_Christenings_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records)"

The persisted `plan_items[].rationale` is the only place that counts — narration is not persisted and search-records never sees it. Correctness turns on the plan item that searches the indexed christenings (collection 1473014, 'England, Births and Christenings'): its persisted rationale must state that the collection is a partial / Legacy index that is not corrected, so a nil there does not prove the christening is absent (and, ideally, that the parish register itself is the fallback). A plan whose reply mentions the quirk while that item's rationale does not fails this point. Paraphrase is fine.
Plan items must include rationale explaining why each record type was chosen for the question — generic rationale ('more records would help') is a fail.
